slides.title: RetailCo Frontline Acceleration
slides.subtitle: Working backwards from a confident new hire in every APAC store
slides.script: We are going to look at RetailCo from the perspective of the person who feels every operating gap first: a new frontline hire. Across 120 stores and 2,000 frontline staff, their first six weeks expose the same issues the COO named: limited floor visibility, uneven manager performance, inconsistent onboarding, and painful scheduling coordination. Our proposal joins Spacesight, Echo, Harbor Wiki, and Alivia into one operating system for the shop floor, so we can work backwards from the experience we want every new hire, manager, and regional leader to have.

slides.text: The new hire experiences every operating gap before headquarters sees it.
slides.kicker: The thing everyone knows but has not said
slides.script: We all know the spreadsheet is not the real shop floor. It is a delayed description of last week, and by the time it arrives on Monday, the new hire has already been confused, coached well or badly, and rostered through whatever coordination process happened behind the scenes. That is the uncomfortable truth: the person with the least context is asked to absorb the most variability. If we solve for that employee, we are not solving a training problem only; we are solving RetailCo’s operating visibility problem.

slides.title: End state: week six feels repeatable, not lucky
slides.statement: Every new hire should know what good looks like, hear it modeled, and be coached from live store reality.
bullets: Spacesight shows what happened on the floor
Echo captures and scores customer conversations
Harbor Wiki stores the best manager playbooks
Alivia packages the rollout proposal
slides.script: Let us start at the end state. By week six, a new hire should not be the product of whichever manager happened to be working that day. They should have seen what good service looks like in their store, heard strong customer conversations, and found the exact RetailCo guidance when they needed it. Spacesight gives us observable floor reality. Echo gives us the voice of the frontline. Harbor Wiki turns what the best managers do into reusable knowledge. Alivia helps us convert that design into a clear client proposal and rollout plan.

slides.title: A day in the end-state store

cards.heading: Before shift

cards.heading: During service
cards.body: Spacesight and Echo capture real customer and floor signals.

cards.heading: After shift

cards.heading: Across stores

slides.script: In the end-state store, the workday feels different. Before the shift, the new hire is not waiting for informal advice; they can look up the RetailCo way. During service, Spacesight sees the floor patterns and Echo hears how conversations actually happen with customers. After the shift, the coaching is anchored in what occurred that day, not a delayed report. Across APAC, the practices from the best store managers stop being trapped locally and become available to every manager and every new employee.

slides.title: Work backwards from week six
slides.statement: The six-week onboarding window becomes the operating test for the entire store system.
bullets: Week six: consistent execution
Weeks three to five: coached practice
Week two: searchable answers
Week one: observed reality
slides.script: Working backwards, week six is where we want confidence and consistency. To get there, weeks three to five must be coached practice, not random exposure. Week two needs searchable answers, because the new hire will ask questions when the right person is not nearby. Week one needs observed reality, because we cannot improve what we cannot see or hear. This is why the deck is not organized by product first. It is organized by the employee journey that reveals whether the operating model is actually working.

slides.title: The three engines behind that journey

cards.heading: See
cards.body: Spacesight turns shop-floor activity into usable in-store vision analytics.

cards.heading: Hear
cards.body: Echo captures and scores what staff actually say to customers.

cards.heading: Bottle
cards.body: Harbor Wiki makes the best store practices searchable and repeatable.

slides.script: The journey is powered by three engines. First, we see the floor with Spacesight, so RetailCo is not dependent on a Monday spreadsheet to understand what happened. Second, we hear the frontline with Echo, so customer conversations can be captured and scored instead of guessed. Third, we bottle the best practices with Harbor Wiki, so the difference between the best and worst manager is no longer just personal craft. Alivia then sits around this as the proposal engine, helping us turn these pieces into one client-ready plan.

slides.title: Today’s delay becomes same-day visibility
slides.statement: The COO’s Monday spreadsheet problem is answered by seeing and hearing store activity as it happens.
bullets: Pain: “I have no idea what actually happens”
Spacesight: floor behavior and movement patterns
Echo: real customer conversation evidence
Outcome: coaching before memory fades
slides.script: The COO said, “I have no idea what actually happens on my shop floor. I get a spreadsheet on Monday about last week.” That is the first gap the new hire feels, because no one can coach today’s behavior from next week’s report. Spacesight addresses the floor visibility part directly by showing what is happening in-store. Echo completes the picture by capturing what staff actually say to customers. Together, they create evidence that managers can use while the shift is still fresh, instead of reconstructing it days later.

slides.title: From captured reality to reusable coaching

steps.label: Capture
steps.text: Spacesight and Echo collect floor and conversation signals.

steps.label: Score
steps.text: Echo highlights what strong customer interactions sound like.

steps.label: Codify
steps.text: Harbor Wiki turns proven behaviors into searchable guidance.

steps.label: Coach
steps.text: Managers use the same evidence and playbooks with new hires.

slides.script: The mechanism matters because this cannot be another disconnected reporting layer. We capture floor and conversation signals with Spacesight and Echo. We score conversations so strong customer interactions become visible, not anecdotal. We codify what works in Harbor Wiki, where managers and new hires can search it at the moment of need. Then we coach from a shared evidence base. That flow is how RetailCo moves from observing isolated excellence to teaching repeatable excellence across 120 stores.

slides.title: The 3x manager gap becomes a playbook gap
slides.statement: When the best store managers outsell the worst by 3x, their methods have to become company assets.
bullets: Pain: “I cannot bottle what they do”
Echo reveals customer-facing behaviors
Spacesight reveals floor-management patterns
Harbor Wiki stores the RetailCo way
slides.script: The second pain is the 3x spread between the best and worst store managers. We should treat that as a knowledge capture problem, not only a performance management problem. Echo helps reveal how the strongest teams talk to customers. Spacesight helps reveal how the floor is being managed when performance is strong. Harbor Wiki then gives RetailCo the place to bottle those behaviors as the RetailCo way. That is how a new hire in a weaker store can still learn from the practices of the strongest managers.

slides.title: What is covered now, and what remains open

rows.right: Spacesight plus Echo create live operating evidence.
Harbor Wiki bottles proven behaviors from top stores.
Harbor Wiki, Echo, and Spacesight standardize learning.
Open item: scheduling workflow needs a connected owner.

slides.script: We want to be explicit about coverage. The visibility issue maps cleanly to Spacesight and Echo. The 3x manager gap maps to Harbor Wiki, supported by what Spacesight and Echo reveal about strong stores. The six-week onboarding inconsistency is addressed by combining searchable knowledge with real coaching evidence. Scheduling is different. None of these products is a roster engine, so we should not pretend it is solved. It is an adjacent workflow that needs an owner on RetailCo’s side and a decision on whether we integrate with, inform, or simply design around the current scheduling process.

slides.title: Alivia turns the design into a proposal RetailCo can act on
slides.statement: The joined-up proposal should define ownership, store scope, evidence, and the first working session.
bullets: Package Spacesight, Echo, and Harbor Wiki together
Clarify the scheduling open item
Define the first-store working session
Align COO, operations, and frontline leaders
slides.script: Alivia’s role is to turn this solution shape into a proposal RetailCo can act on. We do not want four product conversations. We want one operating proposal that says where we start, which stores are involved, what signals we will use, how the playbook gets built, and how onboarding changes during the first six weeks. Alivia also helps us make the scheduling item explicit, so it is not lost in the enthusiasm for visibility and knowledge capture. That gives the COO a practical path from concept to ownership.

slides.title: Who owns the first six weeks at RetailCo?
slides.subtitle: Our ask: name the owner and schedule the working session.
bullets: Confirm the RetailCo owner for frontline onboarding
Select representative APAC stores for discovery
Review current coaching and scheduling workflows
Run a working session on Spacesight, Echo, and Harbor Wiki
slides.script: Our closing ask is simple. We need to know who owns the first six weeks of a frontline employee at RetailCo, because that person or team also owns the clearest path to solving the COO’s four pains. Once that owner is named, we propose a first working session focused on representative APAC stores, current coaching practices, available onboarding material, and the scheduling workflow that remains open. From there, we can shape a joined-up proposal with Spacesight, Echo, Harbor Wiki, and Alivia that starts from the employee experience and works back into operations.

approach.angle: Take the frontline employee's point of view. A new hire's first six weeks is the sharpest version of every problem the COO raised.
approach.device: Start from the end state you are promising and work backwards to today.
approach.opener: Open by naming the thing everyone in the room already knows but has not said.
approach.close: Close by asking who owns this on their side, and proposing the first working session.
